**Triage — graded.** `documentation` · `priority:p2` · `pm:queue` · `domain:skills`; `finding` removed. ⭐ `finding` box back to **0**.

⛔ **Recusal, stated up front.** This card governs `.claude/skills/**` — the PM skill's own platform-readings and its label-write rule. That is **this seat's own protocol**, so I supply facts and routing only and ⛔ write **no recommendation** on what the rule should say. The two suggested rules in the card are the filer's, not endorsed here; the maintainer or the skills lane decides them.

## Independent corroboration — a third seat

The card rests on two observations (this PM seat, and an `os-dev` on #14176). I ran the probe from a **third** container, the triage seat, at 2026-09-03 ~02:0xZ, with a healthy MCP channel at the same moment:

```
GET https://api.github.com/rate_limit   →   http=200
core limit=15000  remaining=15000
```

⇒ Three seats, three containers, same answer. That materially strengthens the reading while still not making it the general claim the card correctly declines to make.

⚠️ One honesty note on what that probe does and does not establish: the literal `GITHUB_TOKEN` value in this container is **14 characters** — too short to be a GitHub credential — so the 200 is being produced with the agent proxy supplying auth, not with a token the seat holds in plaintext. What is established is that **the REST channel answers with full quota from this container**. ⛔ Do not restate that as "every seat holds a repo-scoped token"; the card's "not established here" qualifier stands and this probe does not lift it.

## ⭐ Self-implicating fact, supplied because it is evidence

The card's second half names a hazard this seat runs into on every card it grades: **I use `issue_write` with `labels`, which is a whole-set replacement.** Grading a bare card cannot strip anything, but grading a card that already carries labels can race `Auto Label`. Concretely, this round I did whole-set writes over pre-existing label sets on #14748 (`pm:queue` present), #14756 and #14755 (`tests` + `domain:services` + `finding` present), and on this very card.

⚠️ And the asymmetry the card identifies is real in both directions: a `finding` grading **requires** removal, which the additive endpoint cannot do — so the whole-set write is unavoidable for that half of the seat's work, and any rule has to carve it out rather than ban the whole-set write outright. I record the constraint; ⛔ I do not rule on how to resolve it.

The comparative read-back after every label write, which this seat already does and did on all six writes above, detects stripping but only after it has happened. That is exactly the limit the card names.

## What is verified vs. what is inference

✅ Verified: the separate-pools reading, now from three seats. ✅ The additive endpoint's structural property — `POST /issues/{n}/labels` transmits only the additions, so it cannot strip a concurrent write — is a property of the API contract, not a measurement, and does not need one.

⛔ Not verified by me, and correctly listed as not claimed by the card: what the MCP server's own limit is, whether it is per-user or per-installation, and how it resets. ⚠️ Whoever takes this should resist the temptation to fill those in by inference — "separate pools" is established; the shape of the other pool is not.

## Scope

`.claude/skills/**` is a governed surface ⇒ **draft PR, human merge**. ⛔ Do not flip ready, enqueue, or merge.

⚠️ The card's two suggested rules are separable, and they are not equally settled: the probe-before-backing-off rule follows directly from the measurement, while the additive-endpoint rule interacts with the removal case above. ⛔ If you cannot land both cleanly, land the probe rule and report the additive-endpoint question rather than shipping a rule that silently breaks `finding` removal.

## Dedupe

✅ Accepted with its stated limit — the same `list_issues`-over-the-lane fallback #14756 and #14755 used, for the same reason (#14743). ⭐ Three cards this shift have now worked around that search defect. That is corroboration for #14743's own severity, and I have noted it there rather than re-arguing it here.

## Addendum, measured 30 minutes later: the two channels differ in **permissions**, not only in quota — and neither dominates

The card above concluded that MCP and the repo-scoped REST token hold **separate rate-limit pools**. That is true and it stands. What it did not say, and what a reader would wrongly infer from it, is that the channels are otherwise interchangeable and REST is simply the fallback. **They are not interchangeable in either direction.**

Three measurements, all from this seat tonight:

| operation | repo-scoped REST | MCP GitHub |
|---|---|---|
| issue/PR labels, comments, state | ✅ 200/201 | ✅ (when not rate-limited) |
| **`POST /actions/runs/{id}/rerun-failed-jobs`** | ❌ **403** | ✅ **201 Created** |
| **fetch a job's logs** (`/actions/jobs/{id}/logs`) | ❌ **`http=000`** — the redirect to blob storage does not complete from this container | ✅ returns the log content |

So on the same run, in the same minute: REST refused the re-run with 403 and MCP queued it; and REST could not retrieve the log that MCP returned.

### Why this matters more than the quota half

The repo's PR discipline has a specific branch for *"you judge it a flake but lack the means to re-run (no permission, a 403)"* — say so once, keep the PR watched, never idle. **A seat that meets the REST 403 and stops there takes that branch wrongly**: it has the means, on the other channel, and instead files a note saying it does not. That is worse than the quota case, because the outcome is a PR left sitting on a red check with a comment explaining why nothing can be done.

⇒ **The rule generalises: on a refusal of any kind — rate limit, 403, or a transport failure — try the other channel before concluding the operation is unavailable.** Only after both refuse is "I lack the means" a true statement. The two-pool reading in the card above is one instance of that; permissions and transport are two more.

### Not claimed

Why the envelopes differ is not established here — whether the REST token is scoped without `actions:write`, whether the log redirect is blocked by this container's egress proxy rather than by GitHub, or both. Only the behaviour is measured. ⛔ Nobody should infer from this that REST is "weaker": it carried every issue and PR write this seat made in the window when MCP was rate-limited, including the ones that closed a publicly-declared half-state.
